note: Rules restate Larry Coon's 1999 Salary Cap FAQ. The live page at http://www.cbafaq.com/salarycap99.htm was read on 2026-10-04 (web.archive.org refused connections from this environment; its closest listed snapshot is from 2012). The page's revision history shows the questions used here on roster, injured reserve, 10-day contracts and waivers (Q53, Q62, Q63, Q64) were last revised in 1999, and no later revision touched them; Q17 was revised up to 2005 only for new figures. Facts found only in the 2005 FAQ (the 2005 CBA, which replaced the 1999 agreement from 2005-06) are marked inferred, not sourced. Status values: sourced (stated by the cited source), inferred (reasoned from sourced facts or a later agreement; see note), not found.

active_list_size.note: IR 'allows teams to keep their full complement of 12 players'.

minimum_players_dressed_per_game.note: 'A team must suit up eight players for each game.'

injured_list_max_players.note: 'Teams may have a maximum of three players on IR at one time.' The FAQ treats injured reserve (IR) and injured list (IL) as one status.

maximum_players_under_contract_regular_s.note: 12 active plus at most 3 on IR. The FAQ does not state a 15-player ceiling in words.

minimum_players_under_contract_regular_s.note: After a waiver or IR placement the team has two weeks to get back to 12 players. The FAQ gives no other minimum; the empty-roster charge below 11 players (Q33) is a team-salary rule, not a roster minimum.

refill_window_days.note: 'two weeks to get back to 12 players'.

injured_list_minimum_games.note: 'A player usually must spend at least five games (or until the end of the season if fewer than five games remain) on IR before being activated.'

injured_list_early_activation.value: allowed before five games only if his spot on the active roster has not been filled
injured_list_early_activation.note: FAQ example: Vancouver, Bryant Reeves, December 1999.

injured_list_medical_check.value: cause must be legitimate, but the league does not insist on an independent physician confirming the diagnosis; placing healthy surplus players on IR was common

hardship_exception.value: with league permission a team may temporarily add a 13th active player when a special hardship exists (FAQ example: three players already out for the season with serious injuries)
hardship_exception.note: No games threshold or duration is given.

waiver_period.value: 48 hours for a player released between August 15 and the end of the regular season; 10 days at any other time

claim_priority.value: if more than one team claims, the team with the worst record gets him

claim_priority_early_season_standings.value: previous season's records until December 1, current-season records from December 1
claim_priority_early_season_standings.note: Not found in the 1999 FAQ. The cited glossary describes later agreements; whether the same December 1 switch applied in 2003-04 was not verified.

value: far enough under the salary cap to fit the player's entire salary
a disabled player exception for at least the player's salary
a traded player exception for at least the player's salary
the player's contract is for one or two seasons at the minimum salary
claiming_team_requirement.note: Any one of the four suffices.

claimed_player_contract.value: the claiming team acquires his existing contract and pays the remainder of his salary

claimed_player_bird_clock.value: reset when claimed before clearing waivers
claimed_player_bird_clock.note: The 1999 FAQ counts Bird seasons 'without being waived'; the explicit claimed-player reset is stated only in the 2005 FAQ.

cleared_waivers.value: player may sign with any team; the new team pays only the pro-rated minimum salary and the original team continues to pay the balance
cleared_waivers.note: Set-off (Q52): the waiving team reduces what it owes by one-half of (new salary minus the one-year-veteran minimum; rookie minimum for a rookie).

waiving_team_cap.value: guaranteed salary of a released player stays in the waiving team's team salary; non-guaranteed players count only for what they earned while with the team

playoff_eligibility_cutoff.value: a player waived after March 1 is ineligible for the playoff roster of any team that signs him for the rest of that season

contract_guarantee_date.value: January 10: all contracts become guaranteed for the remainder of that season; a player terminated on or after January 10 is owed the rest of the season's salary (and before then if unfit because of a basketball-related injury)
contract_guarantee_date.note: Arbitration exception (John Starks, 1999-00): in a contract's last season team and player may agree to remove the January 10 guarantee in a buyout (Q57).

length.value: ten days or three games, whichever comes later

first_signing_date_rule.value: January 5, or the first business day thereafter

first_signing_date_2003_04.note: January 5, 2004 was a Monday. Basketball-Reference records the first 2003-04 10-day contracts that day (Orlando: Lee Nailon; Portland: Slavko Vranes).

max_per_player_per_club.note: Two per season with the same team, consecutive or not.

after_second.value: the team may keep the player only by signing him for the remainder of the season; otherwise he leaves when the contract expires

salary.value: the player's minimum salary for his years of service, pro-rated to the days the contract covers
salary.note: Proration wording is from the 2005 FAQ. The 1999 FAQ (Q9) confirms ten-day contracts are minimum-salary contracts and that for a player with five or more seasons the team pays the four-year-veteran minimum and the league the rest, with only the four-year minimum in team salary. Scale: library/2003/league/nba_1999_cba_minimum_salary_scale.json.

counts_on_cap.value: yes; salary earned stays in team salary through June 30 after the contract ends
counts_on_cap.note: Completed-contract wording is from the 2005 FAQ; the 1999 FAQ (Q52) says released non-guaranteed players count for what they earned while with the team. Over-the-cap teams use the minimum salary exception (Q17).

counts_on_roster.value: yes, as one of the 12 active players
counts_on_roster.note: The FAQ says they 'are used to replace players who are on injured reserve'.

signable_with_15_under_contract.note: A 10-day player is an additional contract; with 12 active and 3 on IR no slot is open. The 2005 FAQ's limit (no more 10-day contracts than players on the inactive list) is not in the 1999 FAQ.

bird_rights.value: 10-day contracts do not count toward Bird rights

definition.value: a contract for the remainder of the current season; the only way to keep a player after his second 10-day contract

salary_at_minimum.value: pro-rated minimum based on the fraction of the season remaining when signed

league_pays_part_for_veterans.value: for players with five or more seasons on a one-year, ten-day or rest-of-season minimum contract, the team pays the four-year-veteran minimum and the league the rest; only the four-year minimum counts in team salary

minimum_salary_exception.value: over-the-cap teams may sign minimum-salary contracts of up to two seasons; second-season salary is that season's minimum; also allows minimum-salary players to be acquired by trade without salary matching

minimum_salary_exception_uses.value: no limit on the number of players signed or acquired
minimum_salary_exception_uses.note: Stated in the 2005 FAQ; the 1999 FAQ states no limit either way.

multiyear_from_prorated.value: a multiyear contract starting at the pro-rated minimum pays the full minimum in later seasons

purpose.value: lets a team over the cap acquire one replacement for a disabled player who will be out for the remainder of the season; may also be granted on a player's death

amount.value: lesser of 50% of the injured player's salary or the average salary

approval.value: league approval based on an NBA-designated physician's determination; the FAQ adds that a Board of Governors vote is required
approval.note: Denied: Phoenix (Danny Manning, 1997-98), Orlando (Grant Hill, 2003). Granted: San Antonio (Sean Elliott, 1999), Charlotte (Bobby Phills).

use.value: one player only; sign a free agent for up to one season or absorb salary in a trade like a traded player exception; cannot be split

deadline.value: player disabled July 1 - November 30: replacement within 45 days; disabled December 1 - June 30 and out the following season too: until October 1

return_of_player.value: the disabled player may be activated immediately if he returns early; the replacement or unused exception is unaffected

under_cap_effect.value: counts in team salary while available if the team is under the cap; lost if team salary plus exceptions stays below the cap

calibration_2003_04.counting_note: Counted from Basketball-Reference's 2004 NBA transactions page read on 2026-10-04 (all dated entries parsed).
